title: SoCal sees flooded roads, water rescues as powerful storm drenches region with rain
text:
Los Angeles rain: Powerful storm brings heavy downpours, flooding roads and triggering water rescues - ABC7 Los Angeles 
 Breaking Magnitude 4.4 earthquake strikes Commerce area, USGS says 24/7 Live Los Angeles Orange County Inland Empire Ventura County California Live WEATHER 
 SoCal sees flooded roads, water rescues as powerful storm drenches region with rain 
 Stream Southern California's News Leader and Original Shows 24/7 Last updated: Friday, November 20, 2026 6:42AM GMT Share LOS ANGELES (KABC) -- A powerful storm is drenching Southern California with heavy rain, inundated roads with water and triggering several water rescues.
 First responders have had to rescue multiple drivers stuck along a flooded portion of Vineland Boulevard North Hollywood.
 Out in the City of Industry, a woman had to be rescued from a flooded wash. Crews used a helicopter to pull her out.
 The rain is expected to continue moving east into Orange County and the Inland Empire throughout the day. Evacuation warnings remain place for several burn scars as those areas brace for potential flooding and debris flows.
 ABC7 is tracking all the storm impacts here.
 Key Headlines
 1:33 AM GMT Evacuation warnings lifted for Palisades, Sunset and Hurst fire burn scars 
 Nov 18, 2026, 5:55 PM GMT Flood Watch, Wind Advisory issued ahead of heavy SoCal rainfall 
 Nov 18, 2026, 5:56 PM GMT Rain timeline: Atmospheric river to bring heavy rain 
 Here's how the news is developing. 6:41 AM GMT 
 Firefighters rescue woman from flood control channel in City of Industry 
 Los Angeles County firefighters were busy in the City of Industry Thursday, as rescuers pulled someone out from the fast-moving waters in a flood control channel. Los Angeles County firefighters were busy in the City of Industry Thursday morning, as rescuers pulled someone out from the fast-moving waters in a flood control channel.
 Video published by the department shows a firefighter paramedic being lowered into the water before successfully rescuing the woman.
 AIR7 captured the rescue from overhead, maneuvering around the clouds.
 The county fire department says this was one of many successful swift water rescues by the agency Thursday.
 By Anabel Munoz 5:01 AM GMT 
 LA sees flooded streets and stranded drivers after storm 
 Thursday saw a lot of street flooding in and around Los Angeles and in some cases, drivers were trapped in their cars and had to be rescued. Thursday saw a lot of street flooding in and around Los Angeles and in some cases, drivers were trapped in their cars and had to be rescued.
 A stretch of Vineland Boulevard in North Hollywood looked more like a river Thursday morning, but inside the flooded waters were about half a dozen cars.
 Swift water rescue teams helped drivers out and one person was taken to the hospital.
 A similar scene happened about three and a half miles away in Panorama City where firefighters found several cars in deep water near Hazeltine and Lanark Street.
 And under a bridge along Hollywood Way, near the Burbank airport, several vehicles were left in flooded waters.
 As Southern California enters a very rainy winter brought by a super El Niño, drivers are reminded:
 "If you see downed trees, if you see issues in the public right of way, we're asking all of our residents to report those issues to MyLA311 by calling 311 or using your smartphone application or via the website," said Steve Kang, president of L.A. City Board of Public Works.
 One of the agencies preparing for and responding to storm damage is L.A.'s Department of Public Works.
 "For example our sanitation crews have cleaned and inspected over 40,000 street catch basins, which are basically the gutters on your streets, and also we're mindful of our hillsides, especially in our burn areas, so 70 hillside debris basins have been cleaned," Kang said.
 Public Works dispatched emergency crews to different parts of the San Fernando Valley Thursday. And as the brunt of the super El Niño is still ahead, the city of L.A. is offering resources to stay prepared at dpw.lacity.gov.
 Residents are also reminded that if they need sandbags, those are available at your local fire station.
 By Denise Dador 2:51 AM GMT 
 Tree falls on man's new truck after heavy rain in San Gabriel Valley 
 The owner of a pickup truck in Arcadia said he had just gone back to work after lunch when a tree crashed on top of his recently purchased vehicle. The owner of a pickup truck in Arcadia told Eyewitness News that he was eating his lunch, went back to his electrician job and just a few minutes later, a large tree crashed on top of his recently purchased vehicle.
 "This tree had fallen right on my car right where I was sitting so I'm just glad I wasn't sitting right there. I thought it was AI. I was devastated. Honestly, I just bought it. Definitely lucky I'm glad yeah thank God but it is what it is," said Tim Kiehl.
 The incident happened around 12:15 p.m.
 Kiehl said he had just bought his Dodge Ram two months ago.
 A couple of hours later, crews showed up to clean up the mess.
 This was just one of the incidents that affected the San Gabriel Valley following Thursday's storm.
 In Irwindale, the CHP reported one person was transported to a local hospital in unknown condition following a solo vehicle crash involving a big rig that went over the guard rails on the northbound 605 Freeway and into the riverbed.
 This incident backed up traffic for about a mile heading north on the 605 Freeway, a couple miles south of the 210. The left lanes were expected to remain closed until about 5 p.m.. The right lanes were open during the incident, but traffic was slow.
 The heavy downpour also caused a big problem for residents who lost their homes in the Eaton Fire. As we approach the two-year mark, people running out of rent coverage are finding ways to move back to their property. Altadena Town Councilmember Nic Arnzen says up to 400 people maybe living on their land in RVs and even tents.
 "So the biggest concern is that there's a lot of loose dirt and that loose dirt can turn into mud flows and also creates flows that you don't typically see so people might think they're ready, but I just advised them to make sure they listen to their evacuation warnings," said Arnzen.
 The rain also caused delays for people midway through reconstruction.
 Help is available at the Eaton Fire Collaboratory, where they're organizing sandbag giveaways starting Friday and resources for people who remain displaced and need help getting through the winter.
 1:33 AM GMT 
 Evacuation warnings lifted for Palisades, Sunset and Hurst fire burn scars 
 The evacuation warnings that had been issued for the Palisades, Sunset and Hurst fire burn scars have been lifted, according to the Los Angeles Fire Department.
 The department made the announcement at 4:45 p.m. Thursday.
 The warnings were originally expected to be in effect until Friday morning.
